what: Retrosheet's event notation and the English it must read as. Every front end that expands a play is held to this file.
why: The play-by-play is stored in shorthand and expanded at the moment of reading, because 18,263,689 plays would be 889 MB of stored English. That makes the expansion the one substantial thing a second front end has to reimplement rather than read from the export -- 252 lines, 24 regexes and 7 lookup tables in describePlay. These pairs are the contract, kept out of any one language so a Swift or Kotlin port can be checked against the same sentences the JavaScript is.
how: For each entry in `expanded`, expanding `event` must produce exactly `text`. For each entry in `shorthand`, the parser must decline to translate and show the event as written -- a gap has to read as shorthand on the page, never as a confidently wrong sentence. test_views.js runs this file; see README, What the data can and can't say.

expanded.note: A placeholder for a substitution. Where the sub records are loaded the row says who came in instead; this is what the event alone means.

expanded.text: Ground ball out, third baseman to first baseman.
Home run down the right-field line.
Single to center field. Runner on second scored. Runner on first to third.

expanded.note: Two men handled it and the first is the one who fielded it. The + and - marks are safely ignorable.

expanded.text: Double down the left-field line. Runner on second scored.
Reached on an error by the shortstop.
Double play, shortstop to second baseman to first baseman.
expanded.note: The parenthesised runner is dropped; stripping it is what keeps the third fielder in the chain.

expanded.text: Wild pitch. Runner on second to third.
Home run to extra deep left-center.
expanded.note: Hit locations live inside the trajectory modifier and Retrosheet documents the zones only in a diagram, hitloc.jpg. The grammar below was read off the data: a zone of one or two fielder positions, then a side (L, R, M), a depth (S, D, XD) and F for foul.

expanded.text: Fly ball out to deep center field.
Fly ball out down the right-field line in foul ground.
Line drive out into foul ground by first base.
Ground ball out to the third baseman.
expanded.note: Depth is dropped on a bare infield position: "deep shortstop" is not a place.

expanded.text: Ground ball out, shortstop to first baseman.
expanded.note: A ground ball keeps its chain of fielders, which is already the location.
An unlocated modifier still reads. Before 1989 most batted balls have no location at all.
A location code the grammar does not cover leaves the sentence alone rather than dropping a wrong place into it.

shorthand.note: An event never seen before must come back unread, with the shorthand shown as written. The fallback is the honest half of the parser.
